title: Charts: bar and line
setup:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("games.csv")
explanation: Charts make patterns jump out. Any pandas result can draw itself with .plot(). Use kind="bar" to compare categories (like genres), kind="barh" for sideways bars, and kind="line" to show change over time (like years). Add title="..." to label the chart. The usual recipe: summarise first (value_counts or groupby), then .plot(). The chart appears below your code.

lines.explain: Count the games in each genre.
Draw those counts as a bar chart with a title.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many bars will this chart have?
hints: One bar per value that value_counts() finds.
How many different genres are there?

tasks.prompt: Fill in the blank to draw the genre counts as a bar chart.
hints: The chart type is text, so it needs quotes.

solution_lines.explain: A bar chart, one bar per genre.

tasks.prompt: Draw a line chart of how many games came out each year.
hints: Count per year with groupby, then plot a line.

solution_lines.explain: A line shows the change over time: 2017 stands out.

tasks.prompt: Draw a sideways bar chart of every game's price, with the titles as labels.
hints: On the whole table, plot() takes x= for the labels and y= for the values.

solution_lines.explain: One sideways bar per game. Long titles fit better sideways.

tasks.prompt: Draw a bar chart of the average rating per genre, highest first.

solution_lines.explain: Highest first, so the chart reads like a ranking.
Draw it. Sports has no rating, so it has no bar.

recap: You just learned to draw bar, sideways bar and line charts with .plot(): summarise first, then plot.
